newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Dollar/yen risk reversals snap in.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar/yen risk reversals snap in.

text.p: Risk reversals on dollar/yen options dramatically reduced their bias for yen calls as spot's jump allayed nagging fears of a downturn.

Heavy buying of both dollar/yen spot and longer-dated low delta dollar calls helped pull the one-month risk reversal down to 0.3/0.6 percent, traders said. The risk reversal --which reflects market preference for calls or puts -- stood at 1.1/1.5 for yen calls on Tuesday and a hefty 2.7/3.1 just a week ago.
"The risk reversal has crashed off from last week, and shows the diminished fear of a break lower in spot," said an options dealer at a U.S. bank in London.
In the one-year, the risk reversal now traded at 0.2/0.6 percent for yen calls compared to around 1.0 percent last week, said a strategist at another U.S. bank.
He said the risk reversal move had occurred as the market finally realised its fears of a sharp decline in dollar/yen spot were exaggerated.
"It was ridiculous to have a risk reversal so strongly skewed one way," he said.
Spot dollar/yen hit a peak of 127.46 on May 1 before declining swiftly. It had been ensconced in a 110.50-115.70 range since mid-June but Tuesday saw a sudden upspike to 115.98.

Implied volatilities on dollar/yen options eased slightly to 10.1/10.4 percent in the one-month from Tuesday's late European level of 10.3/10.6 and stayed steady at 10.75/11.05 percent in the one-year.
Spot dollar was quoted at 115.70/80 yen at 1126 GMT compared to 115.88/98 in late Europe yesterday.
Dollar/mark was trading at 1.7920/30, down from the 71-month high of 1.8040 it hit on Tuesday, and implied volatilities took a breather too.
One-month dollar/mark implied vol softened to 10.45/10.7 percent from yesterday's 10.3/10.6.
